tei:titleStmt.tei:title: Keri'at Shema al Hamita: May the pleasantness of my Master, our God, be upon us, and

tei:div.tei:p: May the pleasantness of my Master, our God, be upon us, and the work of our hands be established for us and may the work of our hands—establish it.

tei:note.tei:p: In this closing sentence of Psalm 90, Moses prays that the Divine Presence rest on the Jewish nation exclusively.

David prays first that the service Jewry performs in the Sanctuary, the sacrificial offerings, and the general performance of mitzvos be willingly accepted by God. Then he prays that even the work we do for our own needs be acceptable before Gold.—Iyun T’Filoh
The first mention of work refers to the actual endeavors of our hands, whereas the second mention of work refers to what was achieved by our hands.—Iyun Tefilloh
